about: Meta descriptions for BC pages (no "AP"). AB topics use calculus/data/descriptions.json; an entry here overrides it on the BC page.

lessons.integration-by-parts: Integration by parts, step by step: choose u and dv, run the tabular method, and practice exam-style questions with feedback on each slip.
lessons.partial-fractions: Linear partial fractions, step by step: factor, split into A/(x - a) + B/(x - b), find A and B, and integrate, with exam-style practice.
lessons.improper-integrals: Improper integrals, step by step: rewrite as a limit, evaluate, and decide convergence, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.eulers-method: Euler's method, step by step: take tangent-line steps from a known point, fill the table, and judge over or under, with exam-style practice.
lessons.logistic-models: Logistic models, step by step: carrying capacity, the limit of the solution and the point of fastest growth, with exam-style questions.
lessons.arc-length: Arc length, step by step: from chord lengths to the integral, set up and evaluate lengths of graphs, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.math-parametric-vectors: A quick refresher on parametric equations and vectors before Unit 9: trace a path, eliminate t, and find a vector's length, with practice.
lessons.parametric-derivatives: Parametric derivatives, step by step: dy/dx as (dy/dt)/(dx/dt), tangent lines and horizontal and vertical tangents, with exam-style practice.
lessons.parametric-second-derivatives: Second derivatives of parametric curves, step by step: differentiate dy/dx, divide by dx/dt, read concavity, with exam-style practice.
lessons.parametric-arc-length: Parametric arc length, step by step: integrate the speed over the interval, exact and with a calculator, with exam-style questions.
lessons.vector-derivatives: Vector-valued functions, step by step: velocity and acceleration vectors and speed, with exam-style questions and feedback on each slip.
lessons.vector-integrals: Integrating vector-valued functions, step by step: position from velocity and a starting point, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.planar-motion: Motion in the plane, step by step: speed, position, displacement and total distance for a particle, with free-response style practice.
lessons.math-polar: A quick refresher on polar coordinates before 9.7: plot points, convert to x and y, and read common polar graphs, with practice questions.
lessons.polar-derivatives: Polar derivatives, step by step: dy/dx for r = f(θ), and what dr/dθ says about distance from the origin, with exam-style practice.
lessons.polar-area: Polar area, step by step: one half the integral of r² dθ, limits from the graph, with exam-style questions and feedback on each slip.
lessons.polar-area-between: Area between two polar curves, step by step: find where they meet and subtract the squares, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.math-sequences: A quick refresher before Unit 10: limits of sequences, factorial ratios and sigma notation, with practice questions and feedback.
lessons.series-convergence: Convergent and divergent series, step by step: partial sums and their limit, telescoping sums, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.geometric-series: Geometric series, step by step: find a and r, decide convergence and find the sum, with exam-style questions and feedback on each slip.
lessons.nth-term-test: The nth term test, step by step: when terms not approaching 0 prove divergence and when the test is silent, with exam-style practice.
lessons.integral-test: The integral test, step by step: check the conditions, compute the improper integral and conclude, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.p-series: Harmonic and p-series, step by step: read p, decide convergence and use them as benchmarks, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.comparison-tests: Comparison tests, step by step: pick a benchmark series, run the direct or limit comparison test and conclude, with exam-style practice.
lessons.alternating-series-test: The alternating series test, step by step: check all three conditions and state the conclusion, with exam-style questions and feedback.
lessons.ratio-test: The ratio test, step by step: simplify the ratio, take the limit and read the result, with exam-style questions and feedback on each slip.
lessons.absolute-conditional: Absolute and conditional convergence, step by step: test the absolute values, then the series, and classify it, with exam-style practice.
lessons.alternating-error-bound: The alternating series error bound, step by step: bound the error by the first omitted term and find its sign, with exam-style practice.
lessons.taylor-polynomials: Taylor polynomials, step by step: derivatives at the center, coefficients over factorials and approximations, with exam-style practice.
lessons.lagrange-error-bound: The Lagrange error bound, step by step: justify the maximum M, compute the bound and compare it with the accuracy asked, with practice.
lessons.radius-interval-convergence: Radius and interval of convergence, step by step: the ratio test, then both endpoints checked on their own, with exam-style practice.
lessons.taylor-series: Taylor and Maclaurin series, step by step: build a series from derivatives and use the four known series, with exam-style practice.
lessons.power-series-functions: Representing functions as power series, step by step: substitute, differentiate and integrate known series, with exam-style practice.

notes.integration-by-parts: Integration by parts undoes the product rule: choose u and dv, use the tabular method for repeated parts, and handle integrals like x cos x and ln x.
notes.partial-fractions: Linear partial fractions: split a fraction whose bottom has distinct linear factors into simpler ones, find the constants, then integrate each piece.
notes.improper-integrals: Improper integrals with an infinite limit or an integrand that blows up: write the limit, evaluate it, and decide whether the integral converges or diverges.
notes.eulers-method: Euler's method approximates a solution of a differential equation with tangent-line steps. Build the table and tell an overestimate from an underestimate.
notes.logistic-models: Logistic growth dP/dt = kP(K - P): read the carrying capacity, the limit of P, and the population where it grows fastest, without solving the equation.
notes.arc-length: The length of a curve y = f(x) as the integral of the square root of 1 + (f'(x))², from chords to the formula, with exact and calculator lengths.
notes.math-parametric-vectors: Parametric equations and vectors for Calculus BC: plot a path from t, eliminate the parameter, and find a vector, its components and its length.
notes.parametric-derivatives: Find dy/dx for a parametric curve, tangent lines, and horizontal and vertical tangents, with the slips that cost points on the exam.
notes.parametric-second-derivatives: Second derivatives of parametric curves: differentiate dy/dx with respect to t, then divide by dx/dt, and read concavity from the sign.
notes.parametric-arc-length: Arc length of a parametric curve as the integral of speed: exact and calculator lengths, and what changes when the curve is traced twice.
notes.vector-derivatives: Vector-valued functions: position, velocity and acceleration vectors, speed as the length of velocity, and velocity estimated from a table.
notes.vector-integrals: Position from velocity in the plane: integrate each component, add the starting point, and avoid dropping or subtracting the initial position.
notes.planar-motion: Motion in the plane: speed, position, displacement and distance traveled, direction from dx/dt and dy/dt, as the free-response questions ask them.
notes.math-polar: Polar coordinates for Calculus BC: plot (r, θ), convert with x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, and recognize circles, roses, limaçons and cardioids.
notes.polar-derivatives: Derivatives of polar curves: treat r = f(θ) as a parametric curve to get dy/dx, and read dr/dθ to tell when a point moves toward or away from the origin.
notes.polar-area: Area inside a polar curve as one half the integral of r² dθ: find the limits from where r = 0 or curves meet, and avoid dropping the ½ or the square.
notes.polar-area-between: Area between two polar curves: inside one and outside the other, find where they meet, and integrate one half of (outer² - inner²), not (outer - inner)².
notes.math-sequences: Sequences and their limits, factorials and sigma notation: the tools Unit 10 leans on, with factorial ratios simplified step by step.
notes.series-convergence: What it means for an infinite series to converge: partial sums, their limit, telescoping series, and why the terms alone do not settle it.
notes.geometric-series: Geometric series: find the first term and ratio r, the sum a/(1 - r) when |r| < 1, and series that start at a later index or carry an x.
notes.nth-term-test: The nth term test for divergence: if the terms do not approach 0 the series diverges, and if they do, the test says nothing.
notes.integral-test: The integral test: when the terms come from a positive, continuous, decreasing function, the series and its improper integral converge or diverge together.
notes.p-series: The harmonic series diverges and a p-series converges exactly when p > 1. How to spot one, rewrite roots as powers, and use it as a benchmark.
notes.comparison-tests: The direct and limit comparison tests for series with positive terms: choose a geometric or p-series to compare with and state the conclusion correctly.
notes.alternating-series-test: The alternating series test: terms that alternate in sign, decrease in size and approach 0 give a convergent series. Check and state all three conditions.
notes.ratio-test: The ratio test: the limit of |a(n+1)/a(n)| below 1 converges, above 1 diverges, equal to 1 decides nothing. Best with factorials and powers.
notes.absolute-conditional: Absolute and conditional convergence: test the series of absolute values first, then the series itself, and classify each series in three ways.
notes.alternating-error-bound: The alternating series error bound: the error of a partial sum is at most the first term left out, and the sign of the error comes from that term.
notes.taylor-polynomials: Taylor and Maclaurin polynomials: coefficients from derivatives at the center, divided by k factorial, and how to use them to approximate a value.
notes.lagrange-error-bound: The Lagrange error bound for a Taylor polynomial: find the next derivative, justify its maximum M on the interval, and show the error is small enough.
notes.radius-interval-convergence: Radius and interval of convergence of a power series: the ratio test gives the radius, then each endpoint is tested on its own series.
notes.taylor-series: Taylor and Maclaurin series: the series for e^x, sin x, cos x and 1/(1 - x), where each converges, and how a series is built from derivatives.
notes.power-series-functions: New power series from known ones: substitute, multiply by powers of x, and differentiate or integrate term by term, keeping track of the interval.
notes.choosing-integration-methods: How to choose an antidifferentiation technique on the BC exam: basic rules, substitution, division, completing the square, parts and partial fractions.

units.unit-9: Parametric equations, vector-valued functions and polar curves: derivatives, arc length, motion in the plane and polar area, with free notes and practice.
units.unit-10: Sequences and series: every convergence test, error bounds, Taylor polynomials and series, and intervals of convergence, with free notes and practice.
